name: Bulbasaur
english: Bulbasaur is a combination of bulb (a rounded underground storage organ present in some plants) and dinosaur or ‑saurus (common suffix used in the names of extinct reptilian creatures, derived from the Ancient Greek word for lizard). The name also sounds similar to the word bulbous.
japanese: From 不思議 fushigi (strange, mysterious) and 種 tane (seed), as well as a pun of 不思議だね Fushigi, da ne? (Isn't it strange?)
korean: From 이상하다 isanghada (to be strange or abnormal) and 씨 ssi (seed)
chineseMandarin: From 妙 miào (wonderful), 蛙 wā (frog), and 種子 / 种子 zhǒngzǐ (seed)
chineseCantonese: From 妙 miuh (wonderful), 蛙 wā (frog), and 種子 júngjí (seed); From 奇異 kèihyih (strange) and 種子 júngjí (seed)

name: Ivysaur

chineseCantonese: From 妙 miuh (wonderful), 蛙 wā (frog), and 草 chóu (grass); From 奇異 kèihyih (strange) and 草 chóu (grass)

name: Venusaur
english: Venusaur may be a combination of Venus (referring to the Venus flytrap plant) or venom and dinosaur or ‑saurus (common suffix used in the names of extinct reptilian creatures, derived from the Ancient Greek word for lizard).

Alternatively, in a 2016 interview with Tsunekazu Ishihara by INSIDE, Charmander is stated to be a combination of charcoal (carbon residue produced by strongly heating wood) and Salamandra (a genus of salamander including four species of fire salamander).

name: Ampharos
english: Ampharos may be a combination of amp (a measure of electrical current) and pharos (lighthouse), as well as amparo (Portuguese and Spanish for aid and protection).

name: Marill
english: Marill and Maril may be a combination of mar (Spanish and Portuguese for "sea") or 丸い marui (round or circular) or 鞠 mari (ball), 瑠璃 ruri (lapis lazuli), and possibly rill (a small river or brook) and マリンブルー marine blue.

name: Azumarill
english: Azumarill may be a combination of azure (a shade of blue), azul (Spanish and Portuguese for "blue"), or azul marino (Spanish for "navy blue"), mar (Spanish and Portuguese for "sea") or Marill, and possibly rill (a small river or brook).

korean: Transcription of Japanese name
chineseMandarin: Transcription of Japanese name. Contains 露 lù (dew)
chineseCantonese: Transcription of Japanese name. Contains 露 louh (dew)

name: Hoppip
english: Hoppip may be a combination of hop or hippity-hop and pip (small hard seed) or pipsqueak. The names Hoppip, Skiploom, and Jumpluff are together based on the phrase "hop, skip, and jump".

chineseCantonese: From 毽子 yínjí (shuttlecock) and 草 chóu (grass)

name: Skiploom

japanese: From 張り手 harite (an open-hand slap move in sumo), 張り合う hariau (to compete with), 張り倒す haritaosu (to knock down), 針山 hariyama (pincushion), and 山 yama (mountain)
korean: From the partial transcription of Japanese name and 뭉기다 mung'gida (to throw down, destroy, demolish)
chineseMandarin: From 鐵掌 / 铁掌 tiězhǎng (iron palm) and 力士 lìshì (sumo wrestler); From 超 chāo (super), 力士 lìshì (sumo wrestler), and 王 wáng (king)
chineseCantonese: From 鐵掌 titjéung (iron palm) and 力士 lihksih (sumo wrestler); From 超 chīu (super), 力士 lihksih (sumo wrestler), and 王 wòhng (king)

name: Azurill
english: Azurill may be a combination of azure (a shade of blue) or azul (Spanish and Portuguese for "blue") and rill (a small river or brook). Its name may also be derived from its Evolutions, Marill and Azumarill.
japanese: From 瑠璃 ruri (lapis lazuli)
korean: Transcription of Japanese name
chineseMandarin: Transcription of Japanese name. Contains 露 lù (dew)
chineseCantonese: Transcription of Japanese name. Contains 露 louh (dew)

name: Nosepass
english: Nosepass may be a combination of nose or a corruption of north and compass. NOSE is also a mnemonic for the cardinal directions in French (nord, ouest, sud, est).
japanese: From ノーズ nōzu (nose), ノース nōsu (north), and compass
french: From tarin (slang for nose) and nord (north)
korean: From 코 ko (nose) and compass
chineseMandarin: From 朝北 cháoběi (to face north) and 鼻 bí (nose)
chineseCantonese: From 朝北 chìuhbāk (to face north) and 鼻 beih (nose)

name: Skitty
english: Skitty may be a combination of skittish and kitty.
japanese: From 狗尾草 enokorogusa (green foxtail) and 猫 neko (cat)
korean: From the partial transcription of Japanese name and 나비 nabi (kitty); Transcription of English name
chineseMandarin: From 向尾 xiàng wěi (to face the tail), 狗尾草 gǒuwěicǎo (green foxtail), and 喵 miāo (meow)
chineseCantonese: From 向尾 héung méih (to face the tail), 狗尾草 gáuméihchóu (green foxtail), and 喵 mēu (meow)

name: Delcatty
english: Delcatty may be a combination of delicate and catty.
japanese: From 狗尾草 enokorogusa (green foxtail), 猫 neko (cat), and 心 kokoro (heart)
korean: Transcription of English name
chineseMandarin: From 優雅 / 优雅 yōuyǎ (graceful) and 貓 / 猫 māo (cat)
chineseCantonese: From 優雅 yāungáh (graceful) and 貓 māau (cat)

name: Sableye
english: Sableye may be a combination of sable (either referring to the heraldic color or the animal it is named after) and eye. It may also be a play on able-eyed.
japanese: From 闇 yami (darkness), 恨み urami (grudge, malice), and 睨み nirami (glare)
korean: Corruption of 깜깜 kkam-kkam (dark, pitch-black)
chineseMandarin: From 勾魂 gōuhún (soul-stealing) and 眼 yǎn (eye)
chineseCantonese: From 勾魂 ngāuwàhn (soul-stealing) and 眼 ngáahn (eye)

name: Mawile
english: Mawile may be a combination of maw (jaws of a voracious animal) and wile (cunning stratagem) or smile.
japanese: From 口 kuchi (mouth) and cheat or eat
korean: From 입 ip (mouth) and cheat
chineseMandarin: From 大嘴 dà zuǐ (big mouth) and 娃 wá (doll)
chineseCantonese: From 大嘴 daaih jéui (big mouth) and 娃 wā (doll)

name: Aron
english: Aron may be a combination of armor and iron.
japanese: From 小 ko (small), 子 ko (child), 坑道 kōdō (mining tunnel), and dragon or コドラ Kodora (Lairon)
german: From Stollen (tunnel, tunnel passage) and Junior
korean: From 갑옷 gabot (armor, shell)
chineseMandarin: Transcription of Japanese name
chineseCantonese: Mandarin-based transcription of Japanese name

name: Lairon
english: Lairon may be a combination of lairy (slang for aggressive) or lair and iron.
japanese: From 坑道 kōdō (mining tunnel), 小 ko (small), and dragon
german: From Stollen (tunnel, tunnel passage) and Drache (dragon)
korean: From 갱도 (坑道) gaengdo (mine tunnel) and dragon
chineseMandarin: Transcription of Japanese name
chineseCantonese: Mandarin-based transcription of Japanese name

name: Aggron
english: Aggron may be a combination of aggressive or aggregate and iron.
japanese: From boss, 坑道 kōdō (mining tunnel), and dragon or コドラ Kodora (Lairon)
german: From Stollen (tunnel, tunnel passage) and Koloss (colossus) or boss
korean: Partial transcription of Japanese name
chineseMandarin: From 波士 bōsí (Cantonese for boss) and transcription of Japanese name
chineseCantonese: From 波士 bōsí (Cantonese for boss) and Mandarin-based transcription of Japanese name

name: Meditite
english: Meditite may be a combination of meditate and petite or tyke. It may also involve tight as in tight focus.
japanese: From asana and 軟 nan (soft, flexible)
french: From méditer (to meditate) and tikka (Tilaka, traditional forehead mark located on the third eye chakra)
korean: From yoga and 랑 (郎) rang (young man)
chineseMandarin: Rough transcription of Japanese name
chineseCantonese: Rough transcription of Japanese name

name: Medicham
english: Medicham may be a combination of meditate and champion.
japanese: From charm, harem pants, champion, and possibly challenge
korean: From yoga and harem
chineseMandarin: Transcription of Japanese name
chineseCantonese: Mandarin-based transcription of Japanese name

name: Electrike
english: Electrike may be a combination of electric and lightning strike. It may also involve tyke (dialectical word for mongrel dog; colloquial word for small child).
japanese: From 落雷 rakurai (lightning strike)
french: From dynamique (dynamic) or dynamo (an electrical generator) and volt
german: From Frizel (onomatopoeia for spark discharges) and Blitz (lightning)
korean: From thunder and a partial transcription of the Japanese name
chineseMandarin: From 落雷 luòléi (lightning strike) and 獸 / 兽 shòu (beast) or 雷獸 / 雷兽 léishòu (thunder beast)
chineseCantonese: From 落雷 lohklèuih (lightning strike) and 獸 sau (beast) or 雷獸 lèuihsau (thunder beast)

name: Manectric
english: Manectric may be a combination of mane and electric.
japanese: From 雷 rai (thunder), lion, live, and volt or bolt
korean: From thunderbolt and volt
chineseMandarin: From 雷電 / 雷电 léidiàn (thunder and lightning) and 雷獸 / 雷兽 léishòu
chineseCantonese: From 雷電 lèuihdihn (lightning strike) and 雷獸 lèuihsau

name: Plusle
english: Plusle and Prasle may be derived from plus, possibly in reference to positive electrical charge. It may also be derived from a partial anagram of pulse.
japanese: From plus and possibly pulse
french: From positive and possibly ピカピカ pikapika (Japanese onomatopoeia for sparkling)
korean: From plus
chineseMandarin: From 正電 / 正电 zhèngdiàn (positive charge) and 拍 pāi (clap)
chineseCantonese: From 正電 jingdihn (positive charge) and 拍 paak (clap)

name: Minun
english: Minun may be derived from minus, possibly in reference to negative electrical charge. It may also include bun or bunny.
japanese: From minus
french: From négative (negative) and possibly ピカピカ pikapika (Japanese onomatopoeia for sparkling)
korean: Transcription of its Japanese name
chineseMandarin: From 負電 / 负电 fùdiàn (negative charge) and 拍 pāi (clap)
chineseCantonese: From 正電 fuhdihn (negative charge) and 拍 paak (clap)

name: Volbeat
english: Volbeat may be a combination of volt and beetle or beat.
japanese: From bulb, beat, and beetle
korean: Transcription of its English name
chineseMandarin: From 電 / 电 diàn (electric), 螢 / 萤 yíng (firefly), and 蟲 / 虫 chóng (bug)
chineseCantonese: From 電 dihn (electric), 螢 yìhng (firefly), and 蟲 chùhng (bug)

name: Illumise
english: Illumise may be a combination of illuminate and luciferase (class of enzymes that produces bioluminescence).
japanese: From illuminate and luciferase
french: From lumière (light) and luciole (firefly) or vol (fly)
korean: From neon and beat or beetle
chineseMandarin: From 甜 tián (sweet) and 螢 / 萤 yíng (firefly)
chineseCantonese: From 甜 tìhm (sweet) and 螢 yìhng (firefly)

name: Roselia
english: Roselia may be a combination of rose, azalea, and camellia.
japanese: From rose and azalea or camellia
korean: Transcription of Japanese name
chineseMandarin: From 毒 dú (poison) and 薔薇 / 蔷薇 qiángwéi / qiángwēi (rose)
chineseCantonese: From 毒 duhk (poison) and 薔薇 chèuhngmèih (rose)

name: Gulpin
english: Gulpin may be derived from gulping, sculpin or gulp in. It may also involve toxin.
japanese: From ゴクリ gokuri (in one gulp) and possibly toxin
french: From gloup (onomatopoeia for swallowing) and petit (small)
german: From schlucken (to swallow) and spucken (to spit)
korean: From 꼴깍꼴깍 kkolkkak-kkolkkak (onomatopoeia for gulping) and monster
chineseMandarin: From 溶 róng (to dissolve), 食 shí (to eat) and 獸 / 兽 shòu (beast)
chineseCantonese: From 溶 yùhng (to dissolve), 食 sihk (to eat) and 獸 sau (beast)

name: Swalot
english: Swalot may be a combination of swallow and a lot.
japanese: From 丸呑み marunomi (swallowing whole)
korean: From 꿀꺽꿀꺽 kkulkkeok-kkulkkeok (onomatopoeia for gulping) and monster
chineseMandarin: From 吞食 tūnshí (to devour) and 獸 / 兽 shòu (beast)
chineseCantonese: From 吞食 tānsihk (to devour) and 獸 sau (beast)

name: Carvanha
english: Carvanha may be a combination of carve or carnivore and piranha. It may also involve carnage.
japanese: From 牙 kiba (fang) and ピラニア pirania (piranha)
korean: From sharp and piranha
chineseMandarin: From 利 lì (sharp), 牙 yá (teeth), and 魚 / 鱼 yú (fish)
chineseCantonese: From 利 leih (sharp), 牙 yá (teeth), and 魚 yùh (fish)

name: Sharpedo
english: Sharpedo may be a combination of shark, sharp, and torpedo.
japanese: From 鮫肌 samehada (rough skin, lit. shark skin)
korean: From shark and piranha
chineseMandarin: From 巨 jù (giant), 牙 yá (teeth), and 鯊 / 鲨 shā (shark)
chineseCantonese: From 巨 geuih (giant), 牙 ngàh (teeth), and 鯊 sā'

name: Wailmer
english: Wailmer may be a combination of whale, wail (a prolonged cry), and mer (French for "sea").
japanese: From whale, 吠える hoeru (to bellow), and 子 ko (child)
korean: From 고래 gorae (whale) or 대왕고래 daewanggorae (blue whale) and 왕자 (王子) wangja (prince)
chineseMandarin: From 吼 hǒu (roar) and 鯨 jīng (whale)
chineseCantonese: From 吼 háu (roar) and 鯨 kìhng (whale)

name: Wailord
english: Wailord is a combination of wail (a prolonged cry) and lord. It may also involve whale.
japanese: From whale, 吠える hoeru (to wail, to bellow), and 王 ō (king)
korean: From 고래 gorae (whale) and 왕 (王) wang (king) or 대왕고래 daewanggorae (blue whale)
chineseMandarin: From 吼 hǒu (roar), 鯨 jīng (whale), and 王 wáng (king)
chineseCantonese: From 吼 háu (roar), 鯨 kìhng (whale), and 王 wòhng (king)

name: Numel
english: Numel may be a combination of numb and camel.
japanese: From 鈍 don (dull, slow, stupid) and camel
french: From chamelon (young camel), ballot (silly), as well as a pun on chamallow
korean: From 둔하다 dunhada (slow-witted) and 낙타 (駱駝) nakta (camel)
chineseMandarin: From 呆 dāi (simple-minded), 火 huǒ (fire), and 駝 / 驼 tuó (camel)
chineseCantonese: From 呆 ngòih (simple-minded), 火 fó (fire), and 駝 tòh (camel)

name: Camerupt
english: Camerupt may be a combination of camel and erupt.
japanese: From 爆発 bakuhatsu (explosion or eruption), 駱駝 rakuda (camel), and possibly Bactrian camel
korean: From 폭발 (爆發) pokbal (explosion) and 낙타 (駱駝) nakta (camel)
chineseMandarin: From 噴火 / 喷火 pēnhuǒ (to erupt) and 駝 / 驼 tuó (camel)
chineseCantonese: From 噴火 panfó (to erupt) and 駝 tòh (camel)

name: Torkoal
english: Torkoal and Cotoise may be combinations of tortoise and coal, and a homophone of kotatsu, a Japanese heating table which was traditionally powered by coal. Torkoal's name also happens to overlap with the swedish verb "torkar" which means "to dry."
japanese: From coal and tortoise, homophonous with kotatsu
korean: Transcription of Japanese name
chineseMandarin: From 煤炭 méitàn (coal) and 龜 / 龟 gūi (tortoise)
chineseCantonese: From 煤炭 mùihtaan (coal) and 龜 gwāi (tortoise)

name: Spoink
english: Spoink may be a combination of spring and oink (grunting sound of a pig).
japanese: From 発条 bane (spring) and ブーブー būbū (onomatopoeia for oinking)
korean: From pig and jump
chineseMandarin: From 跳 tiào (to jump) and 豬 / 猪 zhū (pig)
chineseCantonese: From 跳 tiu (to jump) and 豬 jyū (pig)

name: Grumpig
english: Grumpig may be a combination of grumpy and pig. It may also involve grunt (guttural sound of a pig).
japanese: From ブーブー būbū (onomatopoeia for oinking) and pig
french: From groin (pig snout), gros (big), grogner (to grunt), and goret (piglet)
german: From gross (big), grunzen (to grunt), and oink
korean: From pig and king
chineseMandarin: From 噗 pū (onomatopoeia for puffing) and 豬 / 猪 zhū (pig)
chineseCantonese: From 噗 pok (onomatopoeia for puffing) and 豬 jyū (pig)

name: Spinda
english: Spinda may be a combination of spin and panda.
japanese: From patch and reel
korean: From 얼룩 eolluk (spot)
chineseMandarin: From 晃 huàng (to sway) and 斑 bān (spots)
chineseCantonese: From 晃 fóng (to sway) and 斑 bāan (spots)

name: Trapinch
english: Trapinch may be a combination of trap and pinch.
japanese: From nutcracker
korean: From 톱 top (saw) and 치 (齒) chi (tooth)
chineseMandarin: From 大 dà (big), 顎 / 颚 è (jaw), and 蟻 / 蚁 yǐ (ant)
chineseCantonese: From 大 daaih (big), 顎 ngohk (jaw), and 蟻 ngáih (ant)

name: Vibrava
english: Vibrava may be a combination of vibrate (to shake rapidly) and larva. It may also derive from Vibra.
japanese: From vibrate, larva, and Vibra
korean: Transcription of the Japanese name
chineseMandarin: From 超音波 chāoyīnbō (ultrasound) and 幼蟲 / 幼虫 yòuchóng (larva)
chineseCantonese: From 超音波 chīuyāmbō (ultrasound) and 幼蟲 yauchùhng (larva)

name: Flygon
english: Flygon may be a combination of fly and dragon, or an inversion of dragonfly.
japanese: From fly, dragon, and dragonfly
korean: Transcription of Japanese name
chineseMandarin: From 沙漠 shāmò (desert) and 蜻蜓 qīngtíng (dragonfly)
chineseCantonese: From 沙漠 sāmohk (desert) and 蜻蜓 chīngtìhng (dragonfly)

name: Cacnea
english: Cacnea may be a combination of cactus and its Japanese name, or cactus and debonair.
japanese: From 仙人掌 saboten (cactus) and debonair
korean: From 선인장 (仙人掌) seon-in-jang (cactus) and 왕 (王) wang (king)
chineseMandarin: From 刺 cì (spike), 球 qiú (ball), or 刺球 chhì-kiû (Hokkien for cactus), and 仙人掌 xiānrénzhǎng (cactus); From 沙漠 shāmò (desert) and transcription of Japanese name
chineseCantonese: From 刺 chi (spike), 球 kàuh (ball), or 刺球 chhì-kiû (Hokkien for cactus), and 仙人掌 sīnyàhnjéung (cactus); From 沙漠 sāmohk (desert) and transcription of Japanese name

name: Cacturne
english: Cacturne and Noctus may be a combination of cactus and nocturne (French for "nocturnal").
japanese: From nocturne or nocturnal and cactus
korean: From 밤 bam (night) and 선인장 (仙人掌) seon-in-jang (cactus)
chineseMandarin: From 夢 / 梦 mèng (dream), 歌 gē (song), and 仙人掌 xiānrénzhǎng (cactus); From 夢 / 梦 mèng (dream), 歌 gē (song), and 沙漠奈亞 / 沙漠奈亚 Shāmònàiyǎ / Shāmònàiyà (Cacnea (former translation))
chineseCantonese: From 夢 mùhng (dream), 歌 gō (song), and 仙人掌 sīnyàhnjéung (cactus); From 夢 mùhng (dream), 歌 gō (song), and 沙漠奈亞 Sāmohknoih'a (Cacnea (former translation))

name: Swablu
english: Swablu may be a combination of swab (small wad of cotton on a rod) and blue. It may also involve swallow (a type of bird).
japanese: From Mytyl and Tyltyl (protagonists of L'Oiseau Bleu) and cotton, and possibly チル chiru (Ryukyuan for crane) and Tyl (alternate name of Epsilon Draconis)
korean: From 파랑 parang (blue) and possibly beak and cotton
chineseMandarin: From 青鳥 Qīngniǎo (blue bird; the play L'Oiseau bleu) and 綿 / 绵 mián (silk floss; soft)
chineseCantonese: From 青鳥 Chēngníuh (blue bird; the play L'Oiseau bleu) and 綿 mìhn (silk floss; soft)

name: Altaria
english: Altaria may be a combination of alto (Spanish, Portuguese, and Italian for high; musical part between tenor and soprano) and aria (Italian for air; musical piece for a single voice). Both words being terminologies used in music relate to Altaria's singing abilities. The name may also refer to the star Altair (named after the Arabic phrase Al-Nisr Al-Ṭa'ir, "the flying eagle"), the brightest star in the constellation Aquila, with the latter's name being the Latin word for eagle; or the former name of the star Delta Draconis, Altais, a yellow star in the constellation Draco, with the latter's name being the Latin word for dragon.
japanese: From チルット Tyltto (Swablu), Mytyl and Tyltyl (protagonists of L'Oiseau bleu), cockatrice, and possibly チル chiru (Ryukyuan for crane) or Tyl (alternate name of Epsilon Draconis) and Altais (former name of Delta Draconis)
korean: From 파비코 Pabiko (Swablu), 파랑 parang (blue), or 파랑새 Parangsae (dollarbird; the play L'Oiseau Bleu), and possibly beak and 꼬리 kkori (tail)
chineseMandarin: From 七夕 Qīxì (festival whose legend features the stars Altair and Vega, as well as a bridge of magpies) and 青鳥 / 青鸟 Qīngniǎo (blue bird; the play L'Oiseau Bleu)
chineseCantonese: From 七夕 Chātjihk and 青鳥 Chēngníuh (blue bird; the play L'Oiseau Bleu)

name: Zangoose
english: Zangoose may be a combination of 斬 zan (slash) and mongoose. Additionally, the use of Z in Zangoose mirrors the S in Seviper, possibly in reference to their rivalry.
japanese: From 斬 zan (slash) and mongoose
korean: Similar to the Japanese name
chineseMandarin: From 貓鼬 / 猫鼬 māoyòu (mongoose) and 斬 / 斩 zhǎn (slash)
chineseCantonese: From 貓鼬 māauyauh (mongoose) and 斬 jáam (slash)

name: Seviper
english: Seviper may be a combination of sever (to cut and detach), severe (intense) or serpent and viper. Additionally, the use of S in Seviper mirrors the Z in Zangoose, possibly in reference to their rivalry.
japanese: From 波布 habu and snake
korean: Transcription of English name
chineseMandarin: From 飯匙倩 / 饭匙倩 fànchíqiàn (Chinese cobra) and 蛇 shé (snake)
chineseCantonese: From 飯匙倩 faahnchìhsihn (Chinese cobra) and 蛇 sèh (snake)

name: Lunatone
english: Lunatone may be a combination of lunar and stone.
japanese: From luna (Latin for "moon") and stone
korean: Transcription of Japanese name
chineseMandarin: From 月 yuè (moon) and 石 shí (stone)
chineseCantonese: From 月 yuht (moon) and 石 sehk (stone)

name: Solrock
english: Solrock is a combination of solar and rock.
japanese: From sol (Latin for "sun") and rock
korean: Transcription of Japanese name
chineseMandarin: From 太陽 / 太阳 tàiyáng (sun) and 岩 yán (rock)
chineseCantonese: From 太陽 taaiyèuhng (sun) and 岩 ngàahm (rock)

name: Barboach
english: Barboach may be a combination of barb or barbel (whiskerlike sensory organ in a catfish) and loach.
japanese: From 泥鰌 dojō (pond loach) and loach
korean: From 미꾸라지 mikkuraji (loach)
chineseMandarin: From 泥 ní (mud) and 泥鰍 / 泥鳅 níqiū (pond loach)
chineseCantonese: From 泥 nàih (mud) and 泥鰍 nàihchāu (pond loach)

name: Whiscash
english: Whiscash may be a combination of whisker, mustache, and possibly catfish. The first letter of its English name may also come from the "W" shaped symbol on its head.
japanese: From 鯰 namazu (catfish) or 大鯰 Ōnamazu
french: From barbillon (barbel), poisson-chat (catfish), and a pun on barbiche
german: From Wels (catfish) and Barthaar (whisker) or Zar (tsar)
korean: From 메기 megi (catfish) and king
chineseMandarin: From 鯰魚 / 鲶鱼 niányú (catfish) and 王 wáng (king)
chineseCantonese: From 鯰魚 níhmyùh (catfish) and 王 wòhng (king)

name: Corphish
english: Corphish may be a combination of corps (branch of military servicemen) or corporal and crayfish.
japanese: From 兵 hei (soldier), 弊害 heigai (harmful effect), and 蝦蟹 ebigani (crayfish)
french: From écrevisse (crayfish), écraser (to crush), and pince (pincer)

name: Baltoy

korean: From get, hand, both, and 원숭이 wonsung-i (monkey)
chineseMandarin: From 雙 / 双 shuāng (double), 尾 wěi (tail), 怪 guài (strange), and 手 shǒu (hand), forming a parallel to 長尾怪手 / 长尾怪手 Chángwěiguàishǒu (Aipom)
chineseCantonese: From 雙 sēung (double), 尾 méih (tail), 怪 gwaai (strange), and 手 sáu (hand), forming a parallel to 長尾怪手 Chèuhngméihgwaaisáu (Aipom)

name: Drifloon
english: Drifloon may be a combination of drift and balloon.
japanese: From ふわふわ fuwa fuwa (soft, airy and light, onomatopoeia for floating), 風船 fūsen (balloon), and 不安定 fuantei (unstable)
french: From ballon de baudruche (balloon) and dérive (drift)
korean: From 흔들다 heundeulda (to shake or wave), 풍선 (風船) pungseon (balloon), and 손 son (hand)
chineseMandarin: From 飄飄 / 飘飘 piāopiāo (to flutter; unstable; colloquial term for ghost) and 氣球 / 气球 qìqiú (balloon)
chineseCantonese: From 飄飄 pīupīu (to flutter; unstable; colloquial term for ghost) and 氣球 heikàuh (balloon)

name: Drifblim
english: Drifblim may be a combination of drift and blimp.
japanese: From ふわり fuwari (onomatopoeia for gentle floating), ride, and a pun of 附和雷同 fuwaraidō (following blindly)
german: From Drift and Zeppelin (a type of rigid airship)
korean: From 둥실둥실 dungsil-dungsil (buoyantly) and ride
chineseMandarin: From 隨風 / 随风 suífēng (wind-borne) and 氣球 / 气球 qìqiú (balloon); From 附和 fùhè (to go along) and 氣球 / 气球 qìqiú (balloon)
chineseCantonese: From 隨風 chèuihfūng (wind-borne) and 氣球 heikàuh (balloon); From 附和 fuhwoh (to go along) and 氣球 heikàuh (balloon)

name: Buneary
english: Buneary may be a combination of bunny and ear.
japanese: From 耳 mimi (ear) and roll
korean: From ear and roll
chineseMandarin: From 捲 / 卷 juǎn (to roll up) and 耳 ěr (ear)
chineseCantonese: From 捲 gyún (to roll up) and 耳 yíh (ear)

name: Lopunny
english: Lopunny may be a combination of lop (a breed of rabbit with ears that flop over rather than stand erect) and bunny.
japanese: From 耳 mimi (ear) and lop
german: From Schlappohr (floppy ear; colloquial term for bunny)
korean: From ear and lop
chineseMandarin: From 長 / 长 cháng (long), 耳 ěr (ear), and 垂耳兔 chuí'ěrtù (lop rabbit)
chineseCantonese: From 長 chèuhng (long), 耳 yíh (ear), and 垂耳兔 sèuih'yíhtou (lop rabbit)

name: Mismagius
english: Mismagius may be a combination of mischievous or Misdreavus and magus or magic.
japanese: From 夢魔 muma (nightmare; demon in a dream) and 蠱 maji (to bewitch), mage, or magic
korean: From 무우마 Muuma (Misdreavus) and magic
chineseMandarin: From 夢 / 梦 mèng (dream), 妖 yāo (fay), and 魔 mó (demon; magic)
chineseCantonese: From 夢 muhng (dream), 妖 yíu (fay), and 魔 mō (demon; magic)

name: Honchkrow
english: Honchkrow may be a combination of honcho (boss) and crow.
japanese: From Don (crime boss) and 烏 karasu (crow)
french: From corbeau (crow) or Cornèbre (Murkrow), and boss
german: From Krähe (crow), Rabe (raven), Kramurx (Murkrow), and Chef (boss, chief)
korean: From don and crow
chineseMandarin: From 烏鴉 / 乌鸦 wūyā (crow) and 頭頭 / 头头 tóutóu (chief)
chineseCantonese: From 烏鴉 wū'ā (crow) and 頭頭 tàuhtàuh (chief)

name: Glameow
english: Glameow may be a combination of glamour and meow.
japanese: From ニャー nyā (onomatopoeia for meowing) and glamour
korean: From 냐옹 nyaong (onomatopoeia for meowing) and partial transcription of the Japanese name
chineseMandarin: From 魅力 mèilì (glamour, charm) and 喵 miāo (meow)
chineseCantonese: From 魅力 meihlihk (glamour, charm) and 喵 mēu (meow)

name: Purugly
english: Purugly may be a combination of purr and ugly, as well as a play on "pure ugly".
japanese: From デブ debu (fat), 不細工 busaiku (ugly) or ブス busu (ugly person), ニャー nyā (onomatopoeia for meowing), and cat
korean: From 못나다 monnada (to be ugly) and 고양이 goyang-i (cat)
chineseMandarin: From 東施 / 东施 Dōngshī (ugly woman) and 喵 miāo (meow)
chineseCantonese: From 東施 Dūngsī (ugly woman) and 喵 mēu (meow)

name: Chingling
english: Chingling may be a combination of chime, jingling, and -ling (common suffix to denote something that is small or immature).
japanese: From 鈴 rin (bell), りんりん rinrin (onomatopoeia for bell chiming), and しゃんしゃん shanshan (onomatopoeia for bell jingling)
french: Possibly from 子 ko (Japanese for child) and carillon
korean: From 딸랑딸랑 ttallangttallang (onomatopoeia for bell ringing)
chineseMandarin: From 鈴鐺 / 铃铛 língdāng (little bell) and 響 / 响 xiǎng (to make a sound, to ring, or to echo); From 鈴鐺 língdāng (little bell), 噹 dāng (Onomatopoetic sound of bell), and 響 / 响 xiǎng (to make a sound; to ring; to echo)
chineseCantonese: From 鈴鐺 lìhngdōng (little bell) and 響 héung (to make a sound, to ring, or to echo); From 鈴鐺 lìhngdōng (little bell), 噹 dōng (Onomatopoetic sound of bell), and 響 héung (to make a sound; to ring; to echo)

name: Stunky
english: Stunky may be a combination of skunk or stunk and stinky.
japanese: From skunk and プー pū (onomatopoeia of a fart sound )
french: From moufette (striped skunk) and fouetter (slang for "to stink")
korean: From skunk and 뿡 ppung (onomatopoeia of a fart sound)
chineseMandarin: From 臭鼬 chòuyòu (skunk) and 噗 pū (onomatopoeia of a fart sound)
chineseCantonese: From 臭鼬 chauyauh (skunk) and 噗 pok (onomatopoeia of a fart sound)

name: Skuntank
english: Skuntank and Skutank may be a combination of skunk, stank (past tense of stink), and tank.
japanese: From skunk and tank
korean: From skunk and tank
chineseMandarin: From 坦克 tǎnkè (military tank) and 臭鼬 chòuyòu (skunk)
chineseCantonese: From 坦克 táanhāk (military tank) and 臭鼬 chauyauh (skunk)

name: Bronzor
english: Bronzor may be a combination of bronze and mirror.
japanese: From 銅鏡 dōkyō (bronze mirror) and mirror
french: From archéo- (archeo- (prefix for ancient)) and miroir (mirror)
korean: From 동경 (銅鏡) donggyeong (bronze mirror) and mirror
chineseMandarin: From 銅鏡 / 铜镜 tóngjìng (bronze mirror) and 怪 guài (monster)
chineseCantonese: From 銅鏡 tùhnggeng (bronze mirror) and 怪 gwaai (monster)

name: Bronzong
english: Bronzong may be a combination of bronze and gong (a type of musical percussion instrument), dong (onomatopoeia for deep bell reverberation), or bianzhong (an ancient Chinese musical instrument consisting of bells).
japanese: From 銅鐸 dōtaku (bronze bell)
french: From archéo- (archaeo- (prefix for ancient)) and dong (onomatopoeia for bell or gong ringing)
korean: From 동탁 (銅鐸) dongtak (bronze bell), 탁 tak (sound of hitting something hard), and 군 (君) gun (mister)
chineseMandarin: From 青 qīng (blue; green), 青銅 / 青铜 qīngtóng (bronze), and 銅鐘 / 铜钟 tóngzhōng (bronze bell)
chineseCantonese: From 青 chīng (blue; green), 青銅 chīngtùhng (bronze), and 銅鐘 tùhngjūng (bronze bell)

name: Bonsly
english: Bonsly may be a combination of bonsai and sly or lie.
japanese: From 嘘 uso (false) and 鉢 hachi (flowerpot), or a wordplay on 嘘っぱち usoppachi (downright lie)
french: From mini, bonsaï (bonsai), and banzaï (a Japanese cheer or war cry)
korean: From 꼬마 kkoma (little kid) and 거짓 geojit (lie, falsehood)
chineseMandarin: From 盆栽 pénzāi (bonsai), 才怪 cáiguài (expression to indicate something farfetched, equivalent to the slang expression as-if), and 怪 guài (monster); From 愛哭鬼 / 爱哭鬼 àikūguǐ (crybaby) and 樹 / 树 shù (tree)
chineseCantonese: From 盆栽 pùhnchòih (bonsai) and 怪 guài (monster); From 哭 hūk (cry) and 樹 syuh (tree)

name: Mime Jr.
english: Mime Jr. is derived from mime and Jr. (abbreviation of Junior).
japanese: From 真似 mane (mimicry) and nene (Spanish for baby)
korean: From 흉내내기 hyungnaenaegi (mimicry)
chineseMandarin: From 魔 mó (magic) and the transcription of its Japanese name
chineseCantonese: From 魔 mō (magic) and the transcription of its Japanese name

name: Happiny
english: Happiny may be a combination of happiness and tiny or teeny. It may also involve happenstance.
japanese: From pink and 福 fuku (good fortune)
korean: From pink and 복 (福) bok (luck and good fortune) or 행복 (幸福) haengbok (happiness)
chineseMandarin: From 小 xiǎo (small), 福 fú (good fortune), and 蛋 dàn (egg); From 好運 / 好运 hǎoyùn (good luck) and 蛋 dàn (egg)
chineseCantonese: From 小 síu (small), 福 fūk (good fortune), and 蛋 dáan (egg); From 好運 houwahn (good luck) and 蛋 dáan (egg)

name: Chatot
english: Chatot may be a combination of chat and parrot.
japanese: From ぺらぺら perapera (fluently; chatty), parrot, and rap
french: From pie (magpie) and jaco (grey parrot) or jacquot (generic term for any kind of chattering bird)
korean: Transcription of Japanese name
chineseMandarin: From 聒噪 guāzào (noisy) and 鳥 / 鸟 niǎo (bird)
chineseCantonese: From 聒噪 kutchou (noisy) and 鳥 níuh (bird)

name: Spiritomb
english: Spiritomb may be a combination of spirit and tomb. It may also be a play on spiritum (Latin for "spirit").
japanese: From 御影石 mikageishi (granite) and possibly 軽石 karuishi (pumice) and karma
german: From Krypta (crypt), Spuk (apparitions), and possibly the prefix krypto- (indicating "hidden" or "secret", equivalent to English prefix "crypto-")
korean: From 화강암 (花崗岩) hwagang-am (granite) and 돌 dol (stone)
chineseMandarin: From 花崗岩 / 花岗岩 huāgāngyán (granite) and 怪 guài (monster)
chineseCantonese: From 花崗岩 fāgōngngàahm (granite) and 怪 gwaai (monster)

name: Gible
english: Gible may be a combination of gobble and nibble.
japanese: From 鱶 fuka (shark), 丸 maru (round), and a pun of 深まる fukamaru (to deepen)
korean: From deep, 상어 sangeo (shark), and 동 (童) dong (kid)
chineseMandarin: From 圓 / 圆 yuán (round), 陸 / 陆 lù (land), and 鯊 / 鲨 shā (shark)
chineseCantonese: From 圓 yùhn (round), 陸 luhk (land), and 鯊 sā (shark)

name: Gabite
english: Gabite may be a combination of がぶり gaburi (with a big bite) and bite.
japanese: From がぶり gaburi (with a big bite) and bite
french: From Carcharias or Carcharodon and mâcher (chew)
german: From knacken (to crack something), shark, and -sel (German diminutive suffix)
korean: From 한입 han'ip ((in) one bite) and bite
chineseMandarin: From 尖牙 jiānyá (sharp teeth), 陸 / 陆 lù (land), and 鯊 / 鲨 shā (shark)
chineseCantonese: From 尖牙 jīmngàh (sharp teeth), 陸 luhk (land), and 鯊 sā (shark)

name: Garchomp
english: Garchomp may be a combination of its Japanese name, chomp, and possibly gargantuan.
japanese: From がぶり gaburi (with a big bite), Carcharodon carcharias (scientific name of the great white shark), and possibly earth
french: From Carcharodon carcharias (scientific name of the great white shark), carnassier (carnivorous), and croquer (to crunch)
german: From knacken (to crack something) and crack
korean: From 한입 han'ip (in one bite), Carcharodon carcharias (scientific name of the great white shark), and possibly earth
chineseMandarin: From 烈 liè (fierce), 咬 yǎo (to bite), 陸 / 陆 lù (land), and 鯊 / 鲨 shā (shark)
chineseCantonese: From 烈 liht (fierce), 咬 ngáauh (to bite), 陸 luhk (land), and 鯊 sā (shark)

name: Munchlax
english: Munchlax may be a combination of munch (to chew on food) and lax, relax, or Snorlax.
japanese: From カビゴン Kabigon (Snorlax), baby, and possibly 権兵衛 gonbē (common placeholder name for peasants)
korean: From 먹다 meokda (to eat) and 자다 jada (to sleep), where the name literally means "eat, then sleep"
chineseMandarin: From 小 xiǎo (small) and 卡比獸 / 卡比兽 Kǎbǐshòu (Snorlax)
chineseCantonese: From 小 síu (small) and 卡比獸 Kábeihsau (Snorlax)

name: Riolu
english: Riolu is a partial anagram of Lucario, with the ca omitted.
japanese: From a partial anagram of Lucario with the ca omitted
korean: Transcription of Japanese name
chineseMandarin: Transcription of Japanese name
chineseCantonese: Transcription of Japanese name

name: Lucario
english: Lucario may be derived from the reverse of the Japanese transcription of orichalcum (a mythical metal) or oracle (referring to its supernatural abilities involving aura). It may also involve λύκος lúkos (Greek for "wolf"), and possibly luchar (Spanish for "to fight").
japanese: From the reverse of orichalcum, oracle, Canis lupaster lupaster, and λύκος lúkos (Greek for "wolf")
korean: Transcription of Japanese name
chineseMandarin: Transcription of Japanese name
chineseCantonese: Transcription of Japanese name

name: Hippopotas
english: Hippopotas is derived from hippopotamus. It may also incorporate potash, an earthy substance used as fertilizer.
japanese: From hippopotamus
korean: Transcription of Japanese name
chineseMandarin: From 沙 shā (sand) and 河馬 / 河马 hémǎ (hippopotamus); From 怪 shòu (strange) and 河馬 / 河马 hémǎ (hippopotamus)
chineseCantonese: From 沙 sā (sand) and 河馬 hòhmáh (hippopotamus); From 怪 shòu (strange) and 河馬 hòhmáh (hippopotamus)

name: Hippowdon
english: Hippowdon may be a combination of hippopotamus, power, powder (as in sand), or pow (onomatopoeia for a bodily hit), and don (Spanish for "lord") or -don (common suffix in taxonomic names of prehistoric animals derived from the Ancient Greek word for "tooth").
japanese: From 河馬 kaba (hippopotamus) and don (Spanish for "lord; Ancient Greek for "tooth"")
german: From hippopotamus and terra (Latin for ground, earth)
korean: From 하마 hama (hippopotamus) and don (Spanish for "lord; Ancient Greek for "tooth"")
chineseMandarin: From 河馬 / 河马 hémǎ (hippopotamus) and 獸 / 兽 shòu (beast)
chineseCantonese: From 河馬 hòhmáh (hippopotamus) and 獸 sau (beast)

name: Skorupi
english: Skorupi and Scorupi appear to be shortenings of scorpion.
japanese: From a shortening of scorpion
korean: From a shortening of scorpion
chineseMandarin: From 鉗 / 钳 qián (pincers), 尾 wěi (tail), and 蠍 / 蝎 xiē (scorpion); From 紫 zǐ (purple) and 天蠍 / 天蝎 Tiānxiē (Scorpius)
chineseCantonese: From 鉗 kìhm (pincers), 尾 méih (tail), and 蠍 kit (scorpion); From 紫 jí (purple) and 天蠍 Tīnkit (Scorpius)

name: Drapion
english: Drapion and Dorapion may be a combination of dragon, drastic (referring to its violent nature), or Dracula (referring to its huge vampire-looking teeth) and scorpion.
japanese: From dragon, drastic, or Dracula, and scorpion
korean: Transcription of Japanese name
chineseMandarin: From 龍 / 龙 lóng (dragon), 王 wáng (king), and 蠍 / 蝎 xiē (scorpion)
chineseCantonese: From 龍 lùhng (dragon), 王 wòhng (king), and 蠍 kit (scorpion)

name: Croagunk
english: Croagunk may be a combination of croak and gunk (grime).
japanese: From グレる gureru (to turn delinquent) and げろげろ gerogero (onomatopoeia for a frog's croak; exclamation of disgust)
german: From Glibber (slime) and dunkel (dark) or Unke (fire-bellied toad)
korean: From 삐딱하다 ppittakhada (to be poor in behavior) and 개구리 gaeguri (frog)
chineseMandarin: From 不良 bùliáng (bad, harmful) and 蛙 wā (frog)
chineseCantonese: From 不良 bātlèuhng (bad, harmful) and 蛙 wā (frog)

name: Toxicroak
english: Toxicroak may be a combination of toxic and croak.
japanese: From 毒 doku (poison) and frog
korean: From 독 (毒) dok (poison) and 개굴 gaegul (to croak) or 독개구리 deokgaeguri (poison dart frog)
chineseMandarin: From 毒 dú (poison), 骷 kū (skeleton), and 蛙 wā (frog)
chineseCantonese: From 毒 duhk (poison), 骷 fū (skeleton), and 蛙 wā (frog)

name: Carnivine
english: Carnivine may be a combination of carnivore and vine.
japanese: From Dionaea muscipula and 空きっ腹 sukippara (empty stomach) or すきっ歯 sukippa (gap between the teeth)
french: From carnivore, vorace (voracious), and possibly tentacule (tentacle), plante (plante), or tenter (to attract)
korean: From Dionaea muscipula, 틈새 teumsae (gap), and 어금니 eogeumni (molar)
chineseMandarin: From 尖牙 jiān yá (sharp teeth) and 籠 / 笼 lóng (cage) or 豬籠草 / 猪笼草 zhūlóngcǎo (tropical pitcher plant)
chineseCantonese: From 尖牙 jīm ngàh (sharp teeth) and 籠 lúhng (cage) or 豬籠草 jyūlúhngchóu (tropical pitcher plant)

name: Finneon
english: Finneon may be a combination of fin and neon.
japanese: From 蛍光 keikō (fluorescence) and 魚 uo (fish)
korean: From 형광 (螢光) hyeonggwang (fluorescence) and 어 (魚) eo (fish)
chineseMandarin: From 螢光 / 萤光 / 荧光 yíngguāng (fluorescence) and 魚 / 鱼 yú (fish)
chineseCantonese: From 螢光 yìhnggwōng (fluorescence) and 魚 yùh (fish)

name: Lumineon
english: Lumineon may be a combination of luminous and neon.
japanese: From neon and lantern or possibly neon tetra
korean: From neon and light
chineseMandarin: From 霓虹燈 / 霓虹灯 níhóngdēng (neon lamp) or 霓虹燈魚 / 霓虹灯鱼 níhóngdēngyú (neon tetra) and 魚 / 鱼 yú (fish)
chineseCantonese: From 霓虹燈 ngàihhùhngdāng (neon lamp) or 霓虹燈魚 ngàihhùhngdāng'yùh (neon tetra) and 魚 yùh (fish)

name: Mantyke
english: Mantyke may be a combination of manta and tyke (colloquial term for small child).
japanese: From 玉 tama (ball) and manta
korean: Transcription of Japanese name
chineseMandarin: From 小 xiǎo (small), 球 qiú (ball), and 飛魚 / 飞鱼 fēiyú (flying fish)
chineseCantonese: From 小 síu (small), 球 kàuh (ball), and 飛魚 fēiyùh (flying fish)

name: Snover
english: Snover may be a combination of snow and cover, as well as a play on snowed over.
japanese: From 雪 yuki (snow), 頭 kaburi (head) or 被り kaburi (headdress; covering), and possibly 蕪 kabu (turnip)
korean: From 눈 nun (snow) and 쓰개 sseugae (cover, hat)
chineseMandarin: From 雪 xuě (snow), 笠 lì (bamboo rain hat), and 怪 guài (monster)
chineseCantonese: From 雪 syut (snow), 笠 lāp (bamboo rain hat), and 怪 gwaai (monster)

name: Abomasnow
english: Abomasnow may be derived from Abominable Snowman, another name for the Yeti.
japanese: From 雪の王 yuki no ō (snow king)
korean: From 눈 nun (snow), 설 (雪) seol (snow), and 왕 (王) wang (king)
chineseMandarin: From 暴風雪 / 暴风雪 bàofēngxuě (blizzard) and 王 wáng (king)
chineseCantonese: From 暴風雪 bouhfūngsyut (blizzard) and 王 wohng (king)

name: Weavile
english: Weavile may be a combination of , weave, evil, and vile.
japanese: From 魔 ma (demon), maneuver, and ニューラ Nyula (Sneasel)
korean: From 포푸니 Popuni (Sneasel) and a partial transcription of its Japanese name
chineseMandarin: Transcription of Japanese name. Contains 狃 niǔ (to covet)
chineseCantonese: Transcription of Japanese name. Contains 狃 náu (to covet)

name: Magnezone
english: Magnezone may be a combination of magnetic zone (an alternative name for a magnetic field) and Magneton.
japanese: From 磁場 jiba (magnetic field), 自爆 jibaku (self-detonation) and electromagnetic coil
korean: From 자폭 (自爆) japok (self-detonation), 자 (磁) ja (magnetic), and 코일 Coil (Magnemite)
chineseMandarin: From 自爆 zìbào (self-detonation), 磁 cí (magnetic), and 怪 guài (monster)
chineseCantonese: From 自爆 jihbaau (self-detonation), 磁 chìh (magnetic), and 怪 gwaai (monster)

name: Lickilicky
english: Lickilicky may be derived from a repetition of lick or licky.
japanese: From べろ bero (colloquial term for tongue), ベロベロ berobero (onomatopoeia for licking), and べろっと berotto (licking or sticking out one's tongue)
